title: Ascend Analytics launches behind-the-meter asset valuation for data center and large industrial loads
html:
Ascend Analytics ("Ascend"), the leading provider of market intelligence and analytics solutions for the power industry, today announced the addition of behind-the-meter (BTM) asset valuation to its PowerVAL platform, enabling data center and large industrial developers and operators to quantify potential cost savings from an on-site battery.

For data center developers and operators weighing the benefits of on-site storage, the charges layered on top of the energy price are rising faster than the energy itself. Commercial and industrial loads can pay for peak power three separate ways, through a utility demand charge set by the highest interval in each billing month, a capacity charge set by their load during the system's summer peak hours, and a transmission charge set by their load during their own transmission zone's peaks. The three do not reliably coincide, and in the most expensive zones the transmission charge alone exceeds the capacity charge.

A battery behind-the-meter can offset the capacity and transmission charges a load would otherwise pay, provided the coincident peak window is correctly predicted and the battery has the duration to cover it. The same battery in front of the meter and bidding into the PJM capacity market is accredited at only part of its nameplate, currently around half for a four-hour asset and declining as more storage joins the system. Siting behind-the-meter can also reach operation sooner, as front-of-meter interconnection queues have grown by as much as tenfold since 2014.

A key difficulty when it comes to BTM storage development has involved producing a cost savings estimate a lender will accept. To help address the need, Ascend’s behind-the-meter asset valuation combines a facility's own consumption profile and tariff configuration with proprietary long-term capacity and transmission price forecasts, allowing developers to co-optimize retail rate arbitrage, demand charge avoidance and coincident peak avoidance in a single dispatch.

Where most tools treat future capacity and transmission prices as an inflationary adder, Ascend forecasts them directly, drawing on the outlooks it maintains for its market intelligence reports, so a savings projection holds across a project's full life rather than only its first year.

In a modeled case on the large general service tariff from PPL Electric Utilities’ (PPL), a utility serving central and eastern Pennsylvania, a 1 MW battery paired with a 3 MW load cut the load's annual peak demand by 15% against a no-battery case, reducing capacity and transmission costs by half, demand charges by just under 12% and retail energy costs by just under 2%, for an unlevered after-tax internal rate of return of 12%.

"The question for a large load is no longer just what power costs, it is how much of its own peak it can avoid buying in the first place," said Michael Fisher PhD, senior managing director of PowerVAL at Ascend Analytics.

"Storage on the customer side of the meter answers that better than storage in front of it, and the gap widens as accreditation falls if retail cost allocation procedures stay the same," he adds. "What has been missing is a way to value the tradeoffs between peak charges together and forecast them a decade out, which is what turns the logic into a number a lender will underwrite."

Behind-the-meter asset valuation supports standalone storage as well as hybrid storage-and-solar configurations and is available now in PJM and ERCOT.

Learn more at PowerVAL | Ascend Analytics
summary: New PowerVAL capability values storage sited behind a commercial or industrial meter, co-optimizing retail rate, demand charge and coincident peak savings
